body.estimand_functional: \(\widetilde C_N=\{b\in\mathcal B:N\widehat\gamma_N^{-1}d_{H_N}(m_N-b\mathbf1,\{a q_N(r):a\in\mathbb R,\ r\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\})^2\le\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}\), where \(\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) is a certified outward \(N^{-1}\)-approximation to the supremum, over the legal physical set \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\), of the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\).

sampling_model.design: Deterministic quasi-uniform triangular arrays in a fixed bounded Lipschitz domain in \(d\in\{1,2\}\), with \(h_N\asymp N^{-1/d}\) and separation comparable to \(h_N\).
sampling_model.units: The observed units are sites \(s_{i,N}\); uncertainty comes from one centered stationary bivariate Gaussian-field realization evaluated at those sites.
sampling_model.treatment: The continuous exposure is \(X(s_{i,N})\), and the homogeneous conditional slope in \(Y(s)=\beta X(s)+W(s)\) is the target.
sampling_model.overlap: No exposure nugget or nonspatial variation is assumed; identification comes from the smoother signed cross-tail with \(p\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\subset(1/2,1)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the marginal microergodic scale ratio \(\gamma=c_W/c_X\) is estimated by residual quadratic variations; \(p\), \(A\), and the nonmicroergodic ranges are profiled or bounded over their stipulated compact sets.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: High-frequency dissipation of exposure--confounder coherence supplies sufficient identification and motivates spectral adjustment.
Relative local smoothness conditions characterize consistent slope estimability and local differences or Laplacians yield consistent estimators.
Locally preconditioned inversion-free covariance estimators are root-\(N\) consistent and asymptotically normal on multidimensional irregular lattices.
Higher-order quadratic variations consistently estimate Mat\'ern smoothness and microergodic parameters on three structured irregular-design families.
Appropriately filtered smoothed spatial cross-periodograms on lattices are relatively consistent and asymptotically normal.
The scalar Mat\'ern microergodic parameter has root-\(N\) Gaussian behavior uniformly over a compact nuisance range with known smoothness.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without restrictions on identification strength.
A plurality-rule aggregate mode consistently estimates the spatial slope, and valid candidate slopes are asymptotically normal.

body.tldr: Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes separate the causal homogeneous slope from a signed Mat\'ern cross-tail even when its amplitude vanishes and its exponent is unidentified. The actual-design Gaussian experiment and feasible scale studentization support an attainable, design-specific Gaussian profile critical value whose compactified quantile is continuous through zero, strong-amplitude tangent limits, exponent endpoints, and the one-dimensional physical elbow. A certified outward interval computation yields asymptotic lower-envelope coverage exactly \(1-\alpha\), root-\(N\) diameter and risk, while an exact observed-field Gaussian two-point/KL argument gives matching squared-risk and arbitrary-honest-confidence-set expected-diameter lower bounds.

project_justification.gap: Existing spatial fixed-domain theory does not provide uniform coverage through a vanishing signed cross-tail on changing quasi-uniform designs, and generic weak-identification theory does not determine the physically attainable tangent and endpoint calibration for this cone.
project_justification.niche: The note treats only the no-nugget, exact Mat\'ern-smoothness-one-half, deterministic quasi-uniform \(d\le2\) model with a compact parametric signed cross-tail. In that class, exact affine stencils make the observed-design mean curve and covariance geometry finite-dimensional and computable.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the actual-design Gaussian experiment, feasible residual-scale studentization, continuous attainable Gaussian-tube calibration with certified upper approximation, exact asymptotic \(1-\alpha\) lower-envelope coverage, root-\(N\) diameter and squared-risk upper bounds, and matching exact observed-field Gaussian two-point/KL lower bounds.

body.related_work: Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott analyze local inversion-free covariance estimation on irregular spatial designs, and Datta and Stein study consistent spatial-slope estimation; neither provides the attainable profile calibration proved here. Li (2022) studies Bayesian fixed-domain posterior behavior and a Bernstein--von Mises limit for covariance parameters, rather than this frequentist signed-cross-tail slope experiment. Andrews and Mikusheva provide generic weak-identification tools, but not the changing curved cone, physical elbow, or certified continuum optimization. Gneiting, Kleiber and Schlather provide the valid multivariate Mat\'ern spectral family. Burman, Ogburn and Datta supply the conditional PM2.5/COVID county-centroid homogeneous-slope consumer when the note's Gaussian Mat\'ern and quasi-uniform design diagnostics hold.
body.technical_internal_limitation: First differences are insufficient in \(d=2\): the analytic covariance remainder creates an \(O(h_N)\) slope bias and normalized correlations of order \(1/r\) create a logarithmic variance factor. Exact affine annihilation removes the quadratic covariance term and yields summable fourth-difference dependence. Three-scale profile intervals may nevertheless have large constants when \(p_{\min}\) is close to \(1/2\); the proposal claims rate optimality, not an efficient constant.
body.honest_scope: All upper guarantees are restricted to the stated no-nugget, exact Mat\'ern-smoothness-one-half Gaussian model, its compact parametric signed cross-tail, deterministic quasi-uniform designs, and \(d\in\{1,2\}\). They do not cover unknown marginal smoothness, nugget effects, random or broader covariance classes, or efficiency constants. The certified numerical statement uses convergent outward interval representations of the fixed model specification and observed coordinates. The lower bound is proved by an exact observed-field Gaussian two-point/KL calculation on the \(A=0\) Mat\'ern-half submodel and transfers to a broader anchor class only after that class is formally shown to contain this submodel. The Burman--Ogburn--Datta application remains conditional on the stated diagnostics and does not enlarge the mathematical model.
